title: Ukraine Strikes St. Petersburg Oil Terminal + Corvette Boikiy at Kronstadt During SPIEF Opening Day — Day 1,560
detail: On June 3, 2026 — Day 1,560 of Russia's full-scale invasion — Ukraine launched one of its most strategically significant deep-strike operations of the war: drones targeted St. Petersburg's oil terminal and the Kronstadt naval base on the opening day of Putin's flagship St. Petersburg International Economic Forum (SPIEF), often called 'Russia's Davos.' Three districts of St. Petersburg were targeted, per city governor Aleksandr Beglov. Most significantly, drones struck the guided-missile corvette Boikiy while in dry dock at Kronstadt naval base — the first confirmed strike on a Russian naval vessel in the Gulf of Finland and a major escalation in geographic scope. The St. Petersburg oil terminal — one of Russia's largest oil transshipment complexes in northwestern Russia — was set ablaze. Separately, Ukrainian drones struck a weapons manufacturing plant in the Tambov region (~600 km from Ukraine's border) and critical infrastructure in Smolensk. Russia's MoD claimed air defenses intercepted 354 Ukrainian drones overnight, making this one of the largest single Ukrainian drone operations of 2026. Several people were wounded in St. Petersburg; no confirmed civilian deaths from the city strike itself. The timing of the attack — coinciding exactly with the SPIEF opening ceremony — appeared designed for maximum strategic embarrassment of the Kremlin's diplomatic showcase. Ukraine's 2026 drone campaign has now struck targets across northwestern, central, and southern Russia, hitting air defense systems, oil infrastructure, military-industrial facilities, and naval assets.

title: Russian Attacks Kill 14+ Across Kharkiv (3), Donetsk (5), and Kherson (6) Regions — Day 1,560
detail: On June 3, 2026 — Day 1,560 of Russia's full-scale invasion — Russian forces continued their sustained campaign of strikes against Ukrainian civilian infrastructure and populated areas across multiple regions. In Kharkiv Oblast, Kharkiv city and 17 other settlements came under Russian attack; at least 3 civilians were killed. The attacks continued Russia's pattern of targeting Ukraine's second-largest city with guided aerial bombs and drones, which has now resulted in more than 20 strikes on Kharkiv in April–June 2026 alone. In Donetsk Oblast, Russian strikes killed 5 residents and wounded 11 — attacks concentrated around frontline communities still under Ukrainian control. In Kherson Oblast, 6 people were killed and 26 injured, including a child, from Russian strikes over the preceding 24 hours. Kherson Oblast continues to face daily Russian attacks across the Dnipro River from Russian-controlled positions on the eastern bank. The combined toll of at least 14 killed across three regions on June 3 underscores Russia's sustained attritional campaign targeting both frontline and rear areas of Ukraine. ISW's June 3 assessment noted that Russian forces failed in their attempt to encircle Lyman and advance on Slovyansk, with the Russian Summer 2026 offensive described as exceedingly unlikely to achieve significant gains in the Slovyansk direction.

title: Ukrainian MoD: 1,130 Russian Troops Eliminated in 24 Hours — Cumulative Losses Reach ~1,368,040 — Day 1,560
detail: On June 3, 2026 — Day 1,560 of Russia's full-scale invasion — Ukraine's General Staff reported approximately 1,130 Russian personnel eliminated in the preceding 24 hours, bringing cumulative losses since February 24, 2022 to approximately 1,368,040 personnel (killed, wounded, missing combined — Ukrainian estimate). The 1,130 daily figure on June 3 is lower than the June 2 figure of 1,440, reflecting reduced frontline intensity on June 3 as Russian forces partially regrouped following heavy losses in Pokrovsk and Huliaipole sectors. The ISW June 3 assessment confirmed no advances by either side across the theater. Russian forces failed in their sustained attempt to encircle Lyman — described by ISW as exceedingly unlikely to achieve Slovyansk direction gains in the Summer 2026 offensive. The cumulative loss figure of ~1,368,040 is a Ukrainian estimate; Western intelligence (Netherlands MIVD April 2026) estimated 1.2 million permanent losses including 500,000+ dead.

media.caption: Russian cumulative losses reach ~1,368,040 with 1,130 eliminated in 24 hours — Day 1,560, June 3, 2026
